_README: PLACEHOLDER — one synthetic case, committed so CI exercises the curated-case
path end to end. It is NOT real feedback and it calibrates nothing.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
Curated cases are the only ones carrying a real `decision_id`, which is the
key a judge verdict joins to a human's thumbs-up/down on the same decision
(eval/judge_calibration.py). That whole path had never run in CI, so it
silently rotted: every curated case scored 0.0 on tool trajectory because
the replay demanded the agent extract 'New prospect' as a customer name.
This file makes CI run the path on every build so that cannot recur —
which is why the case below deliberately keeps the unnamed-prospect
placeholder name. See tests/eval/test_case_source.py.
WHAT IT DOES AND DOES NOT PROVE
Proves : candidates load -> cases reconstruct -> the agent replays them ->
the harvest is written -> judges score it and tag the verdict with
a decision_id.
Does not prove: anything about judge quality. `decision_id` below is a
fabricated zero-id that joins to no human label, so calibration
will correctly report 0 aligned pairs for it.
WHAT A LATER DEVELOPER SHOULD DO
1. Once real human feedback exists, curate it locally:
python3 scripts/curate_feedback.py --out eval/data/feedback_candidates.json
That file is gitignored — it derives from feedback_data/, which is too.
2. Run the loop against it (see 'Scoring curated production cases' in
eval/README.md) and check calibration reports a real `n`.
3. To widen CI coverage, promote a few REVIEWED cases into this file —
one recommend and one escalate exercises both judges. Review each for
customer-identifying data first: whatever lands here is in git forever.
Keep this _README block; the loader ignores unknown keys.
